data.why: The interface takes pasted text input only (a text_area) with three built-in one-click example passages (Nostalgia, Dread, Turning) and a hero passage already embedded in app.py; there is no file upload and nothing to seed.

goals: Paste a literary passage and generate its emotion color palette to see which hues dominate its tone
Inspect the sentence-by-sentence emotional arc chart to find where tension rises or eases across a passage
Read the fingerprint strip of a full passage to compare its emotional shape to other texts at a glance
Identify the dominant emotion and its intensity score for a given passage
Trace which specific keywords in the text are driving each sentence's emotional classification
Compare how a passage's emotional structure differs when switching between fast (lexicon) and precise modes

review.summary: The tree follows the interface's real layout well, from input through whole-passage summaries, the per-sentence arc and word-level attribution, and its replayed screens largely match. It needs fixes before filing: the method-comparison phase describes a silent fallback rather than a Claude analysis, f1 gets the fingerprint's colour encoding wrong, several hover claims cite screens that show no tooltip, and long-text fingerprinting, the README's main use, was never exercised.
